title: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%
contentObjective: I can write and interpret percents greater than 100% and less than 1%.
languageObjective: I can explain my reasoning using the words percent, greater than 100%, less than 1%, and equivalent.

noticeAndWonder.context: The arcade leaderboard shows one player scored 150% of the weekly goal, while a rare bonus round only adds a 0.5% point boost. How can a score be more than the whole goal, and how tiny is a 0.5% boost?
wonderStarters: I wonder what would happen if…

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Power-Up Boost
revealWordProblem.text: In the arcade game, your base score is 80 points. A rare power-up boosts your score to 250% of your base. How many points do you have after the power-up? (Hint: 250% means 2.5 times the base.)
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 250% = 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5, so 2.5 × 80 = 200 points. Because 250% is greater than 100%, the new score (200) is more than the base score (80).

turnAndTalk.question: The leaderboard shows one player hit 150% of the goal and a bonus round gives a 0.5% boost. How can a percent be more than the whole, and how can one be a tiny sliver?
turnAndTalk.kernel: 150% is more than one whole, and 0.5% is a tiny piece smaller than 1%.

stems.en: ___% means ___ because it is more / less than 100%.
stems.es: ___% significa ___ porque es más / menos que 100%.

stems.en: A percent over 100% means ___, and a percent under 1% means ___.
stems.es: Un porcentaje mayor que 100% significa ___, y uno menor que 1% significa ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students explain 150% is more than one whole (the player beat the goal) and 0.5% is far less than one whole (a tiny boost), connecting to the idea of 100% as the whole.
turnAndTalk.extend: 100% means the whole goal. Explain why scoring 150% does NOT mean the player made an error, but scoring '150% correct on a test' usually would.
extendStems: 150% of a goal makes sense because ___.
150% on a test does not make sense because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: When you wrote percents like 150% and 0.5% as decimals, what did you notice about their size compared to 1?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Percents over 100% become decimals bigger than 1, and percents under 1% become decimals close to 0.

stems.en: Percents over 100% have decimals ___ than 1, and percents under 1% have decimals ___.
stems.es: Los porcentajes mayores que 100% tienen decimales ___ que 1, y los menores que 1% tienen decimales ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students state 150% = 1.5 (greater than 1) and 0.5% = 0.005 (much less than 0.01), and recognize these forms are equivalent.
turnAndTalk.extend: Why does 0.5% turn into 0.005 and not 0.05? Explain the role of dividing by 100, and write 150% as a mixed number too.
extendStems: 150% as a mixed number is ___ because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: A jackpot pays 250% of your tokens and you inserted 40 tokens. One friend says 100 tokens, another says 60. Who is right, and why does '250%' mean more than your tokens?
turnAndTalk.kernel: 250% of 40 is 2.5 times 40, which is 100 tokens.

stems.en: The friend who said ___ tokens is correct because 250% = ___ times the whole.
stems.es: El amigo que dijo ___ fichas tiene razón porque 250% = ___ veces el entero.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students convert 250% to 2.5, multiply 2.5 x 40 = 100, and explain that over 100% means more than the original 40 tokens.
turnAndTalk.extend: The friend who said 60 found 150% of 40. Explain the mistake they likely made, and describe a jackpot percent that WOULD give exactly 40 tokens.
extendStems: You would get exactly 40 tokens when the jackpot is ___% because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice on Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%, what strategy did you use when a problem felt tricky?
turnAndTalk.kernel: To change any percent to a decimal, divide by 100 (move the decimal point two places to the left).

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming a specific strategy tied to 6.AT.4 — not just "I multiplied." They should connect steps to the key idea.
turnAndTalk.extend: How would you help a classmate who made the common mistake from today's lesson? Use one vocabulary word.

The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

launch.narrative: The arcade just posted its monthly leaderboard! Some players crushed the target score — one player hit 150% of the goal! Meanwhile, a rare bonus round gives only a 0.5% point boost. You need to understand what these unusual percents really mean to read the leaderboard correctly.

Can a percent be less than 1%? What would that look like?
wonderPrompts: How do you write a percent greater than 100% as a decimal or fraction?
When would you see a percent less than 1% in real life?

conceptIntro.heading: How can a percent be more than the whole, or smaller than a tiny piece?
conceptIntro.intro: 100% means one whole. A percent greater than 100% is more than the whole. A percent less than 1% is a very tiny part.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: To change any percent to a decimal, divide by 100 (move the decimal point two places to the left).

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: A bonus round gives a 0.5% point boost. Write 0.5% as a decimal.

workedExample.label: Final answer
workedExample.work: 0.5% = 0.5, so the boost is 50% — half the points!

optional.correctWork: 0.5% does NOT equal 0.5. To change a percent to a decimal, divide by 100 (move the decimal two places left): 0.5 ÷ 100 = 0.005. So 0.5% = 0.005, a tiny boost far less than 1% — not a huge 50% boost.
hints: Changing a percent to a decimal means dividing by 100, not just erasing the % sign.
0.5% is less than 1%, so its decimal must be less than 0.01. The answer 0.5 is way too big.

approaching.stem: Which of the following is greater than 100%?
approaching.explanation: 1.25 = 125%, which is greater than 100%. The other values are all less than 1 (less than 100%).
choiceFeedback: A percent greater than 100% is more than a whole.
Review which percents are greater than 100%.
hints: 100% equals exactly 1 whole. A value greater than 100% must be greater than 1.
Rewrite each choice as a decimal and ask: is it more than 1?
Test 0.75 first — it is less than 1, so it is under 100%. Check 3/4, 1.25, and 99/100 the same way.

approaching.stem: What is 200% written as a decimal?
approaching.explanation: 200% ÷ 100 = 2.0. Percents greater than 100% become decimals greater than 1.
choiceFeedback: Divide 200 by 100, or move the decimal point left 2 places.
200% is twice as much, so the decimal should be 2 point something.
Remember: a percent is per 100.
hints: 200% is more than 100%, so its decimal must be bigger than 1 — that rules out any tiny decimal.
Percent → decimal: divide by 100 (slide the decimal point two places left).
Start at 200. and hop the decimal two places left: 200 → 20.0 → one more hop lands where?

approaching.stem: What is 0.5% written as a decimal?
approaching.explanation: 0.5% ÷ 100 = 0.005. Move the decimal two places to the left.
choiceFeedback: Divide 0.5 by 100 carefully — move the decimal left 2 places.
0.5% is a very small percent, so the decimal should be tiny.
Check where the decimal point moves.
hints: 0.5% is LESS than 1%, so the decimal must be smaller than 0.01 — a very tiny number.
Divide the percent by 100: move the decimal point two places to the left, adding zeros as needed.
Start at 0.5 and slide the decimal left: 0.5 → 0.05 → one more hop. How many zeros appear?

approaching.explanation: 0.75% is less than 1%. All the other choices are greater than 1%.
choiceFeedback: A percent less than 1% is very small — less than 1/100.
Check: is this percent smaller than 1%?
Look for the smallest percent.
hints: You're hunting for a percent SMALLER than 1% — the number before the % sign must be less than 1.
Compare each percent's number to 1: 7.5, 75, and 1.5 are all bigger than 1. What about 0.75?
Check 0.75%: is 0.75 less than 1? Then compare it against the other three the same way.

approaching.instructions: Sort each value: is the percent greater than 100%, between 1% and 100%, or less than 1%?
hints: Convert each value to a percent first: decimals multiply by 100, and fractions divide top by bottom first.
After converting, sort: over 100% means the decimal was over 1; under 1% means the decimal was under 0.01.
Try 2.5 first: 2.5 × 100 = 250%, which is greater than 100%. Now convert 0.003 and the fractions the same way.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Attempt
workedExample.work: Since 120% has three digits, the student writes 12.0 instead of dividing by 100.

approaching.correctWork: 120% means 120 out of 100. Divide by 100 (move the decimal point two places to the left): 120 ÷ 100 = 1.2. So 120% = 1.2, which makes sense because it is only a little more than one whole (100%).
hints: Dividing by 100 always moves the decimal point two places to the left, no matter how many digits the percent has.
1.2 is only slightly more than 1 whole, matching 120% being only slightly more than 100%. 12.0 would mean 1,200% — way too big.

onLevel.instructions: Match each value to its equivalent percent.
hints: Every match is the same move: decimal × 100 = percent. Fractions become decimals first (top ÷ bottom).
Multiply each decimal by 100 by sliding the decimal point two places right, then find that percent card.
Start with 1.5: slide the decimal two places right to get its percent. Then 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5 tells you which card 3/2 pairs with.

onLevel.stem: A player scored 0.4% of the bonus points. Which decimal represents this percent?
onLevel.explanation: 0.4% = 0.4 ÷ 100 = 0.004. Move the decimal point two places to the left.
choiceFeedback: Move the decimal point left 2 places in 0.4%.
Check your decimal conversion carefully.
hints: 0.4% is less than 1%, so the matching decimal must be smaller than 0.01.
Divide the percent by 100: the decimal point moves two places left, and zeros fill the gaps.
Start at 0.4 and hop the decimal left twice: 0.4 → 0.04 → one more hop gives the answer's form.

onLevel.instructions: Convert each percent to a decimal and a fraction.
hints: The finished row shows the pattern: 150% → 1.5 → 3/2. Percents over 100% give decimals over 1; tiny percents give tiny decimals.
Percent → decimal: divide by 100. Decimal → fraction: write it over a power of 10 (or over 200, 400) and simplify.
Row 2: 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5 for the decimal. Then write 2.5 as 25/10 and simplify. Use the same steps for 0.5% and 0.25%.

onLevel.label: Place these percents on a number line from 0 to 3: A = 50%, B = 150%, C = 275%
hints: This number line runs 0 to 3, so percents above 100% will land past the 1 mark.
Convert each percent to a decimal (divide by 100), then place that decimal on the line.
A: 50 ÷ 100 = 0.5, so A sits halfway between 0 and 1. Convert B and C the same way before placing them.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A rare item has a 0.8% drop chance. Write 0.8% as a decimal.

workedExample.label: Attempt
workedExample.work: The student divides 0.8 by 10 instead of 100, moving the decimal only one place.

onLevel.correctWork: To change a percent to a decimal, always divide by 100 — move the decimal point TWO places to the left, not one. 0.8 ÷ 100 = 0.008. So 0.8% = 0.008, which is far less than 1% (0.01), matching the tiny drop chance in the problem.
hints: Dividing by 100 moves the decimal two places, not one — dividing by 10 is a different operation.
0.08 would actually mean 8%, which is much bigger than the tiny 0.8% drop chance described in the problem.

extending.title: Find the Percent Error

workedExample.label: Move the decimal two places left

extending.correctWork: 0.6% means 0.6 out of 100. Move the decimal two places left: 0.6 → 0.006. The correct answer is 0.6% = 0.006.
hints: The student only moved the decimal one place instead of two.
0.6% is less than 1%, so the decimal must be less than 0.01. 0.06 is too large.

extending.prompt: A game character has 300% of its original health after picking up a power-up. If the original health was 80 points, how many health points does the character have now? A student says 240 points. Another says 380 points. Who is correct and why?
extending.sentenceFrame: The student who said ___ is correct because 300% means ___ times the original, so ___ × 80 = ___.
extending.hint: If the character has 300% health after the power-up, think: what does 300% mean compared to 100%?
hints: 300% is three whole 100%'s — the health got MORE than the original, not less.
Convert 300% to a decimal (divide by 100), then multiply that decimal by the original 80 points.
Write 300% as 300 ÷ 100 = 3.0. Multiply 3.0 × 80 and compare your result with each student's claim.

extending.instructions: A bacteria population starts at 500. Complete the table showing what each percent of the original population equals.
hints: The finished row shows the recipe: turn the percent into a decimal, then multiply by 500.
Percent → decimal (divide by 100), then decimal × 500 = number of bacteria.
For 175%: write 175 ÷ 100 = 1.75, so the calculation is 1.75 × 500. Do 0.5% and 300% the same way.

optionalActivity.intro: The arcade's leaderboard is full of wild percents — sort the tiny boosts from the giant jackpots, then figure out what each one really means!

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1% is treating every percent-to-decimal conversion the same way regardless of size — for example, writing 150% as 0.15 (as if it were an ordinary under-100% percent) instead of 1.5, or writing 0.5% as 0.5 (forgetting to divide by 100 at all) instead of 0.005. Before finalizing an answer, check that the decimal for any percent over 100% is greater than 1, and the decimal for any percent under 1% is less than 0.01.
